summary: Iteration 16: Stripe Payment Link integration backend tests. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration16_payment_link.py with 8 tests covering the new payment-link endpoint, webhook handler for Stripe-hosted Payment Link purchases, _provision_after_payment idempotency, and regression of existing checkout/status endpoints. Result: 6/8 PASS, 2/8 FAIL — both failures are the SAME root-cause backend bug in /app/backend/routers/fulfillment.py:205. Regression: /app/backend/tests/test_user_isolation_fuzz.py 10/10 PASS unchanged.

critical.issue: Webhook handler returns 500 (not 200) when sc.get_checkout_status() fails for a session id Stripe doesn't recognise. The spec says errors must be swallowed/logged so Stripe doesn't retry-storm the endpoint. Root cause: routers/fulfillment.py line 205 calls `sc.get_checkout_status(session_id)` OUTSIDE the try/except block (lines 206-216), and the try/except only catches HTTPException — but the wrapper raises `emergentintegrations.payments.stripe.checkout.CheckoutError`, which is uncaught and becomes a 500. Two of my tests fail for this reason: test_payment_link_webhook_provisions_via_customer_details and test_webhook_idempotent_at_event_level. The stripe_events row never gets a chance to be checked for the duplicate-suppression assertion because the first response is already 500. Impact: in production, Stripe will retry-storm the webhook on any transient `retrieve` failure (rate-limited, race condition where the session isn't queryable yet, etc.) and our event-level idempotency dedupe never runs because the insert happens BEFORE the failing call — wait, actually the insert IS before the failing call (lines 176-180), so subsequent retries will be deduped — BUT the FIRST retry still leaks a 500 to Stripe.

action_items:
Fix /app/backend/routers/fulfillment.py stripe_webhook(): move `status_obj = await sc.get_checkout_status(session_id)` INSIDE the try block (or add a broader try around it) and widen the except to catch `Exception` (or specifically `CheckoutError`). Suggested patch:
```python
    if session_id and payment_status == "paid":
        customer_details = raw_obj.get("customer_details") or {}
        customer_email = customer_details.get("email") or raw_obj.get("customer_email") or ""
        customer_name = customer_details.get("name") or ""
        payment_link_id = raw_obj.get("payment_link") or ""
        if payment_link_id and STRIPE_PAYMENT_LINK_ID and payment_link_id != STRIPE_PAYMENT_LINK_ID:
            print(f"[stripe webhook] payment_link mismatch...")
        source = "payment_link" if payment_link_id else "checkout_session"
        try:
            status_obj = await sc.get_checkout_status(session_id)
            await _provision_after_payment(
                session_id, status_obj,
                email_override=customer_email or None,
                name_override=customer_name or None,
                source=source,
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"[stripe webhook] provision failed for {session_id}: {exc}")
```
After the fix, retest the 2 failing tests in test_iteration16_payment_link.py — they should both pass.

rca_of_the_issue: Backend bug — fulfillment.py stripe_webhook: `sc.get_checkout_status(session_id)` (line 205) is called BEFORE the try/except (lines 206-216) AND the except only catches HTTPException. The Stripe wrapper raises emergentintegrations.payments.stripe.checkout.CheckoutError when the session is missing, so the exception is uncaught and FastAPI returns 500. The spec contract says: 'the webhook still returns 200 (errors are swallowed and logged)' — so this is a regression. Reproduction: POST {id:'evt_x', type:'checkout.session.completed', data:{object:{id:'cs_test_unknown', payment_status:'paid', payment_link:'plink_X', customer_details:{email:'x@example.com'}}}} to /api/webhook/stripe — get 500 with 'Failed to retrieve session status: No such checkout.session'. Mitigation: move get_checkout_status inside the try and widen except to `Exception` (Stripe webhook handlers should NEVER raise — Stripe will retry-storm otherwise). One-line fix shown in action_items.
